clue.text: One member of the family finds this telling

definitions.meaning: a kinsman or kinswoman, someone related by blood or marriage
the act of recounting a story, a narration

explanation.surface: A family member turns out to be good at storytelling.
explanation.definitionFit: The word covers both a kinsman and the narrating of events, as in the relation of a tale.

clue.text: Note a young woman can be thoughtless

parts.note: re is the second note of the sol-fa scale
a miss is a young unmarried woman

explanation.surface: A girl may act without consideration.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can be' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Remiss means negligent or careless, failing to take proper care.

clue.text: Immature creatures, though they may well become high-fliers

definitions.text: Immature creatures, though they may well become high-fliers

parts.words: Immature creatures, though they may well become high-fliers
parts.note: young grubs and caterpillars that grow into winged insects, high-fliers taken literally rather than as achievers

explanation.surface: Youngsters who might one day be top achievers.
explanation.definitionFit: These are the grub stage of insects, many of which later grow wings and fly.

clue.text: Implied a beast backed it

indicators.note: backed says the word for the beast is read in the reverse direction

parts.note: a cat is a beast, an animal

explanation.surface: A creature tacitly supported something.
explanation.walkthrough: 'backed' turns CAT into TAC; 'a' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Tacit means understood without being stated, so implied.

clue.text: Duck restrict the view

parts.note: a duck is a score of nothing in cricket, the letter O
to pinion is to bind or restrain the arms

explanation.surface: A bird blocks the scenery.
explanation.walkthrough: A duck in cricket is a score of zero, hence O.
explanation.definitionFit: An opinion is a belief or viewpoint, what someone takes as their view.

clue.text: A fool assumes it's wrong to help

parts.note: an ass is a fool, a silly person

indicators.note: wrong suggests the letters of the word it's are set out in the wrong order

explanation.surface: Someone presumes a helping hand would be a mistake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'assumes' is only a link meaning takes on, and 'wrong' is the anagram signal for the contraction it's.
explanation.definitionFit: To assist is to give aid or support, a plain synonym for helping.

clue.text: Always in the black, so may be cut

indicators.note: in says one piece is placed inside the other

parts.note: sable is black in heraldry
ever means always

explanation.surface: Being permanently in credit means spending can be trimmed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the black' suggests solvency, but sable is the heraldic word for black; EVER goes inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Severable means able to be severed, divided or cut off.

clue.text: Anger can make one rattier

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one

indicators.note: can make says the letters of rattier can be formed into something new

explanation.surface: Rage may leave someone even more irritable.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can make' is the anagram signal; 'one' gives a Roman numeral placed in front, not inside the scramble.
explanation.definitionFit: To irritate is to annoy or provoke, to anger as a verb.

clue.text: The purest mortal times afford Is spotless reputation (; Richard II)

definitions.text: The purest mortal times afford Is spotless reputation

parts.words: The purest mortal times afford Is spotless reputation
parts.note: a line from Mowbray's speech in Shakespeare's Richard II with one word left blank for the solver to supply

explanation.surface: A quotation from Shakespeare about the value of a good name.
explanation.walkthrough: The full line reads 'The purest ___ mortal times afford / Is spotless reputation'; the gap after 'purest' is the entry.
explanation.definitionFit: Mowbray says that an untarnished name is the purest valuable that life can offer.

clue.text: Material that's most important about a legendary bird

indicators.note: about here means surrounding, so one piece wraps round another

parts.note: main means chief or most important
the roc is the giant bird of Arabian legend, as in Sinbad

explanation.surface: A fabric whose key feature concerns a mythical bird.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' wraps the chief word around 'a' plus the bird, which sit just after its first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Marocain is a crinkled crepe dress fabric, so it is a kind of cloth.

clue.text: Unwilling to declare a point

parts.note: to aver is to state or declare firmly
SE, south-east, is a point of the compass

explanation.surface: Someone reluctant to make a statement.
explanation.definitionFit: Being averse means being opposed or reluctant, hence unwilling.

clue.text: A little cottage, dark and dank and very old

indicators.note: A little says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A small, gloomy, damp and ancient country home.
explanation.walkthrough: The draft took 'and dank and very old' as the definition; only 'very old' defines, the rest is surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Aged means elderly, having lived a long time.

clue.text: Extraordinary cast-filled up with pastry

indicators.note: filled up with says one word is packed inside the other

parts.note: to sling is to throw or cast
a tart is a pastry dish

explanation.surface: An actors' troupe has eaten its fill of pies, remarkably.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cast' looks like a theatre company but is a verb, to throw; 'filled up with' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Something startling is surprising or astonishing, so out of the ordinary.

clue.text: Speeds, resulting in charges being made

definitions.meaning: prices or fees, also local property taxes in Britain

explanation.surface: Fast driving ends with fines being imposed.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both paces of movement and prices or local taxes levied.

clue.text: Shock some almost unshockable people

indicators.note: some says only a portion of the following words is taken, a run of their letters

explanation.surface: Even nearly unflappable folk can be jolted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'some' takes letters across the end of 'almost' and the start of 'unshockable'; 'people' only rounds off the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: To stun is to daze or astound, a synonym for shock as a verb.

clue.text: Will meant to reform after the trial

indicators.note: after places the rearranged letters following the trial

parts.note: a test is a trial

indicators.note: to reform says the letters of meant are formed again in a new order

explanation.surface: Someone resolved to mend their ways once in court.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to reform' is the anagram signal, and 'after' puts the rearranged letters behind the trial.
explanation.definitionFit: A testament is a legal will, as in last will and testament.

clue.text: A sportsman should be among animals, he argues

indicators.note: be among says one piece sits in the middle of the other

parts.note: deer are animals, the word serving as its own plural
a bat is a batsman in cricket

explanation.surface: A sportsman ought to mix with wildlife, he contends.
explanation.walkthrough: BAT, cricket shorthand for a batsman, goes inside DEER.
explanation.definitionFit: A debater is a person who argues a case in formal discussion.

clue.text: Peers receiving dull church dignitaries

indicators.note: receiving says the first piece takes the second into itself

parts.note: peers means looks closely, as one who pries
mat or matt describes a dull, unglossy finish

explanation.surface: Members of the House of Lords welcome boring bishops.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Peers' looks like lords of the realm but is a verb meaning looks closely; 'receiving' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Primates are archbishops, the senior bishops of a church province.

clue.text: Value a really quiet lift

parts.note: pp, pianissimo, is the musical mark for very soft
to raise is to lift

explanation.surface: Treasure a truly silent elevator.
explanation.definitionFit: To appraise is to assess the worth of something, to value it.

clue.text: The new priest, having nothing in, lay up

indicators.note: in, with having, says one piece goes inside the other
new suggests the letters of priest are made into a fresh arrangement

parts.note: O is the round figure for nothing, zero

explanation.surface: A newly arrived clergyman, owning nothing, stored things away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'new' rearranges PRIEST into REPSIT, and 'having nothing in' puts O inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: To reposit is to store or deposit something, lay it up for later.

clue.text: Mark requires a little time

definitions.meaning: a check mark against an item on a list
a moment, as in just a second

explanation.surface: A sign needs only a moment.
explanation.definitionFit: It is both the check symbol made on a list and a British word for an instant, as in back in a tick.

clue.text: Bank getting tied in a knot?

definitions.meaning: a ridge of rock or sand just below the sea surface
the ... knot, the square knot used for tying ... points

explanation.surface: A riverbank being bound up in a tangle.
explanation.definitionFit: A sandbar or ridge of rock is one sense; the other is the square knot sailors tie when shortening sail.

clue.text: Get back about a hundred too much

parts.note: re means about, concerning
C is the Roman numeral for a hundred
over means in excess, too much

explanation.surface: Recoup roughly a hundred more than needed.
explanation.definitionFit: To recover is to regain or retrieve something lost.

clue.text: Trail a loose rope

indicators.note: loose says the letters of trail and a are set free from their order

explanation.surface: Follow an untied cord.
explanation.walkthrough: 'loose' looks like an adjective for the rope but rearranges TRAIL A.
explanation.definitionFit: A lariat is a lasso, a long noosed rope.

clue.text: The engraver's drink?

definitions.meaning: an engraver is, as the 's says, one who chases or embosses metal
a drink taken after another, especially a mild one after spirits

explanation.surface: What does a metalworker like to drink?
explanation.definitionFit: It is both a craftsman who chases designs into metal and a drink taken straight after another.

clue.text: Figure melody's essential for a girl of song

parts.note: M is the Roman numeral for a thousand, a figure
an aria is a melody, especially an operatic solo

explanation.surface: A tune is vital for a singing lass.
explanation.walkthrough: 'essential for' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Maria is the heroine of famous songs, such as the one from West Side Story.

clue.text: Male fish or insect

parts.note: a cock is a male bird
the roach is a freshwater fish

explanation.surface: A choice between a male, a fish or a bug.
explanation.definitionFit: A cockroach is a common scavenging insect.

clue.text: Genuine man wanting an empire

parts.note: real means genuine

indicators.note: wanting means lacking, so letters are dropped from the word man

parts.note: the letters of an are those removed

explanation.surface: An authentic fellow desires an empire.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wanting' looks like desiring but means lacking: MAN without AN leaves M.
explanation.definitionFit: A realm is a kingdom or domain, ruled territory such as an empire.

clue.text: Made bad deal, it followed

indicators.note: made bad says the letters of deal and it are spoilt, put out of order

explanation.surface: Someone struck a poor bargain and then trailed along behind.
explanation.definitionFit: To tail someone is to shadow them, so tailed means followed.

clue.text: Ram going round through barred enclosures

indicators.note: going round says the first piece circles the second

parts.note: Aries is the ram of the zodiac
via means by way of, through

explanation.surface: A ram circles through fenced pens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ram' is the zodiac sign, and 'going round' makes it enclose the word for through.
explanation.definitionFit: Aviaries are large cages for birds, enclosures with bars or mesh.

clue.text: Keep quiet about warm covering

indicators.note: about says the first piece goes around the second

parts.note: sh is the call to keep quiet
to heat is to warm

explanation.surface: Say nothing about a cosy layer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'warm' is a verb here, and 'about' makes the hush word enclose it.
explanation.definitionFit: A sheath is a close-fitting case or cover, as for a blade.

clue.text: Sharper reminder

definitions.meaning: one who gives forgotten lines to actors in a theatre

explanation.surface: A sharper nudge to the memory.
explanation.definitionFit: It is the comparative of an adjective meaning quick, and also the theatre worker who cues actors who forget lines.
